tally.headline: 2 of 11 gradeable claims held up, 5 did not

implied_side.why: EdgeDesk’s own number sat 5.8 points toward Philadelphia Eagles of the quote EdgeDesk captured at DraftKings. That is what the disagreement implied. It was published as research, not as a recommendation to bet it.

implied_total.why: EdgeDesk’s fair total of 45.4 sat 3.1 points below the captured total of 48.5.

closing_line.why: no closing line is held for this game: the Collective captured none and the schedule feed carries none. Closing-line value is left blank rather than estimated from the result.

reasons: 2 claims held up, 4 held up in direction only and 3 did not. Parts of the read were right and parts were not.
EdgeDesk projected a home margin of 2.8 and the game finished 17 the away way — 19.8 points of margin error, OUTSIDE the range the model published.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

verdict.line: The number did not land and the reasoning half held. There is something here to investigate without concluding the model is broken.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 2 published claims said the same thing: EdgeDesk prices this game at Philadelphia Eagles −3.0 with a fair total of 45.5, which makes Philadelphia Eagles the better team here by that margin on this field. EdgeDesk makes it Philadelphia Eagles −3.0 where the market has Philadelphia Eagles −3.0 at DraftKings — a 0.2 points disagreement.
lessons.actual_result: Philadelphia Eagles lost by 17 where EdgeDesk projected a 2.8-point edge. Philadelphia Eagles lost by 17.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk named Philadelphia Eagles as better in market and the game went the other way, across 2 separate published claims. One game does not overturn a season-long rating, but this is the direction to watch: Dallas Cowboys won the game outright
lessons.suggested_investigation: These claims carried 3 points of the published number between them and were contradicted. Check whether the same category has been contradicted in other games this season before touching anything.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 3 of the claims in this article rested on model, home_field.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver; home advantage is priced into the number and cannot be isolated from one game’s box score..
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for model, home_field.

lessons.pregame_expectation: The model published an outcome range of -14.0 → +20.0 (Philadelphia Eagles).
lessons.actual_result: The game finished outside it, at a margin of 17.
lessons.lesson: The published range is meant to contain eight results in ten. A miss is expected roughly twice in ten games and is only a problem in aggregate — which is exactly what this store exists to measure.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Count range misses across the season. A rate materially above 20% means the model’s stated uncertainty is too narrow.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk makes it Philadelphia Eagles −3.0 where the market has Philadelphia Eagles −3.0 at DraftKings — a 0.2 points disagreement.
lessons.actual_result: Philadelphia Eagles lost by 17. the result landed on the market’s side of the disagreement
lessons.lesson: The market had the better estimate here. EdgeDesk’s disagreement was not information on this game, and the honest reading is that the price already contained what the model thought it had found.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Track disagreements of this size across the season. The question is not whether one landed; it is whether the class of them has any edge at all.
